cirithungol_1_0.title: The Green Light
cirithungol_1_0.text: Beneath a brown sky that no longer lets the sun be seen, you go on southward to a crossroads in the middle of a ring of trees. There you take the road that climbs east, towards the mountains. It leads you into a cold valley where everything glows with a sickly green light: the river, the meadows and, at the far end, a city of pale walls with a tall tower crowned with light. You have no intention of going near. Up the northern wall of the valley climbs a path of hewn steps, and in its dust you see small footprints once again.

cirithungol_2_0.title: The Pale Flowers
cirithungol_2_0.text: You skirt the valley through the meadows that run down to the river, seeking the foot of the path without passing near the city. The meadows are covered in white flowers that glimmer faintly in the gloom, like little moons, and smell of rot, of an open grave. The river runs black and soundless. You dare not drink from it, thirsty though you are. You wrap yourself in your cloak and walk quickly, eyes lowered, while the green light follows you over the grass.

cirithungol_2_1.title: The Valley Patrol
cirithungol_2_1.text: You begin to climb the path and at the first bend come face to face with two orcs coming down. They are not like those of the mountains: they wear black mail and on their breasts a painted device, a white moon with a skull for a face. They stop dead and sniff the air. One says something in a hoarse voice and laughs; the other has already drawn a long, curved knife. They stand between you and the climb, and they have no thought of moving aside.

cirithungol_3_0.title: The Orc at the Stream
cirithungol_3_0.text: A stream comes down from the heights and crosses the meadows to join the river. Its water is so cold that your ankles ache as you wade it, and it has the same greenish sheen as everything else. Halfway across you hear a splash upstream: an orc with the white moon on his breast has crouched to fill a bucket. He raises his head, sees you and drops the bucket, which floats away. He runs at you through the water, sword already out.

cirithungol_3_1.title: Webbed Clefts
cirithungol_3_1.text: To keep off the path, where you might meet someone, you climb the clefts in the wall, clutching at roots and ledges. The clefts are full of grey cobwebs, old and dusty, so thick they look like rags. As you brush one aside with your hand, something moves within. Two spiders the size of dogs come out of the cleft, black and hairy, with eyes that gleam like beads. One drops down above your head. The other cuts off your retreat.

cirithungol_3_2.title: The Straight Stair
cirithungol_3_2.text: The path becomes a straight stair, hewn in the rock, climbing on and on without rest into the darkness. The steps are high and narrow, worn in the middle. There is no rail, nothing to hold on to, only the wall on one side and the drop on the other. You climb counting steps until you lose count. Your legs are burning. When you turn to look, the city of the green light lies far below, small as a toy.

cirithungol_3_3.title: The Silence of the Valley
cirithungol_3_3.text: You hide among some rocks to wait for the danger to pass. After a while you realise that you can hear nothing: no wind, no water, no bird, not even your own breathing. You clap your hands and the sound dies in the air as if it had never been. The green light of the city rises and falls slowly, like the pulse of something asleep. You do not know how long you stay like that. When at last you rise, your hands are numb.

cirithungol_4_0.title: The Post of the Moon
cirithungol_4_0.text: Beside the path stands an ancient guard-post of white stone, built by folk far better than orcs. Above the door a crescent moon was once carved, beautiful, but someone has hacked at it and painted a skull over it. Inside there are animal bones, ashes and filth. You sit for a moment on the threshold. You think that this valley, before the green light, must have been a place where the moon was mirrored in the river.

cirithungol_4_1.title: The Collapse
cirithungol_4_1.text: Higher up, a stretch of the path has fallen away, and between the two sides there is a gap too wide to leap. Above it, in the wall, a horn of rock juts out. You cast the grey Elven rope, catch it on the horn at the second try and swing across, your feet against the rock and the abyss beneath. On the other side you give a sharp tug, and the rope comes loose and falls into your hands. You coil it carefully.

cirithungol_4_2.title: The Fire in the Niche
cirithungol_4_2.text: You go on climbing to a landing and see a reddish light: in a niche in the wall, four orcs of the white moon are warming themselves at a small fire, arguing loudly about something that has happened above. You press yourself against the rock to slip past. But the wind shifts, carries your scent to them, and the voices fall suddenly silent. Four heads turn towards the darkness where you stand. One takes up a burning brand and comes closer, sniffing.

cirithungol_4_3.title: The Fleeing Orc
cirithungol_4_3.text: You hear footsteps running down and press yourself into a crack in the wall. An orc passes right by you without seeing you, stumbling, looking back over his shoulder. His helm is askew and there is blood on his arm, and he mutters something over and over, like a madman. He is not fleeing from you: he is fleeing from something above. He drops a curved knife on the steps and does not even stop to pick it up. You wait until his footsteps fade below before going on.

cirithungol_4_4.title: The Falling Stones
cirithungol_4_4.text: You keep climbing, step by step. Suddenly there is a sharp crack above, and then a growing din: stones bouncing down the stair, some as big as heads. You flatten yourself against the wall while they whistle past a hand's breadth from you and vanish into the void. One grazes your shoulder and leaves your arm numb for a good while. When the noise stops, you stay still, waiting for the next. It does not come. You will never know whether they fell of their own accord.

cirithungol_4_5.title: The Gorge of Webs
cirithungol_4_5.text: To spare yourself a stretch of stair, you cut through a narrow gorge between two walls. It is a mistake. The gorge is blocked from side to side by cobwebs, one after another, like the sails of a ship. You cut the first with your sword; it is tough and sticky as wet leather. As you cut the second, the whole gorge trembles. Four spiders come swiftly down the threads from the shadows above, clacking their jaws. Behind you, the webs already close the way.

cirithungol_4_6.title: The Counted Cakes
cirithungol_4_6.text: You sit down in the shelter of a rock and open your pack. You count what is left of the Elves' bread: three cakes, still wrapped in their leaves. You break one, eat half of it slowly and put the rest away. The taste brings back to you for a moment the golden light of the trees, the water of the silver stream, the serene voice of the Lady. You feel stronger than you ought to. You take a sip from your waterskin and set off again.

cirithungol_4_7.title: The Searching Light
cirithungol_4_7.text: You lean over the edge to look at the valley. At that moment the light of the tower grows stronger, and a green beam unfolds and sweeps slowly across the walls, like a hand groping in the dark. It draws near you. You throw yourself behind a rock and curl up, not breathing. The beam passes overhead, lights the stone beside you with a sickly gleam and moves on. You wait for it to die out completely before you move again.

cirithungol_5_0.title: The Ridge
cirithungol_5_0.text: At last you reach the top of the climb. Before you the mountain rises in a jagged ridge, black against the brown sky, and in it opens a cleft: the pass. Beside it, perched upon the rocks, stands a dark tower with a single window lit red. From here you see no guards on its walls, but neither do you know whether they are watching you. You resolve that, come what may, you will not pass beneath that tower if you can help it.

cirithungol_5_1.title: The Stench
cirithungol_5_1.text: The air changes. You begin to notice a sweet, rotten smell unlike anything you know, growing thicker at every step. Among the rocks lie the bones of goats, of wolves and of orcs, empty and clean, as if something had sucked the life from them and cast away the rest. Grey threads are tangled in them. You cover your nose with your cloak. You do not wish to know what feeds like this, but you suspect you soon will.

cirithungol_5_2.title: The Ledge
cirithungol_5_2.text: Exhausted, you look for a place to sleep and find only a narrow ledge, little wider than your shoulders, above the void. You pass the Elven rope around a spike of rock and around your waist, and lie on your side against the wall. You sleep fitfully, waking every time a stone falls. No dawn comes, only a brownish grey a little paler than before. You untie the rope, coil it and put it away, and go on climbing.

cirithungol_5_3.title: The Fumes
cirithungol_5_3.text: A thick pall of fumes comes down from the pass and crawls over the hillside, driven by an east wind. It smells of sulphur and burnt iron, and it makes your eyes stream. You tie a cloth over your mouth and go forward almost blindly, feeling the wall with one hand. You cough until your chest aches. When at last you come out of the smoke, your face is black with soot and your mouth bitter. It is the first breath of the land that lies beyond.

cirithungol_6_0.title: The Black Mouth
cirithungol_6_0.text: The path is lost among rocks and you follow it to the end. There, in the wall, opens a black mouth, taller than two men, from which comes a cold and fetid air. Above, a dark tower perched on the ridge, with a red window, watches the pass; you do not wish to go beneath it, and there is no other way east. Torn webs hang across the threshold, as if someone had broken through them not long ago, and on the stone there are greenish stains, dried. You draw a deep breath, grip your sword and go in.
cirithungol_6_0.choiceLabel: Seek a pass in the rocks

cirithungol_6_1.title: The Brood
cirithungol_6_1.text: You turn off the path into a hollow among the rocks, so that no one can see you from above. The ground is covered in dry husks, like those of enormous eggs, and threads that stick to your boots. Too late you understand that it is a nest. Three young spiders, the size of calves, come out from beneath a slab and slowly surround you, raising their forelegs. Their sweet, rotten smell fills the hollow.

cirithungol_7_0.title: Shelob
cirithungol_7_0.text: In the end only one way remains: the tunnel that runs through the mountain. Inside, the darkness is complete and the stench unbearable. You go forward feeling along the wall, among webs that cling to your face. Then you hear an enormous scraping, a click, and ahead of you two clusters of eyes kindle, one of them dull and crusted, wounded not long ago. A gigantic spider fills the tunnel from side to side. It is Shelob, the ancient mistress of this tunnel, and she is hungry.
